0.1 This Indian Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 28 December 1987, after rhe draft finalized by the Electrical Measuring Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 This revised standard incorporates various modifications particularly for the requirements of rating, infinity adjustment, bump and vibration test. and high voltage test. 0.3 It is recognized that for insulation resistance testers for use in hazardous and stringent environmental conditions, special provisions concerning environmentel testing may be necessary. It is recommended that in such cases, these requirements should be additionally specified. 0.4 The scope of this hand-operated insulation standard is confined to resistance testers. Mains-

1. SCOPE 1.1 This -standard covers direct-reading portable insulation resistance testers ( hand-operated ), enclosing in the same case, a generator having a rated voltage up to 5 kV. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, ing definitions shall apply. the follow-

2.3.1 The range of resistance value from l/l 000 up to l/IO of the rated resistance value, shall be termed as first effective iange and the range of resistance from l/IO of the rated resistance to the rated resistance value is termed the second effective range. 2.4 Central Scale Mark - The scale mark corresponding to l/50 of the rated resistance with the scale values of I, 2, 5 or an integral power of IO or multiples thereof. 2.5 Error in Indication - The difference between the indicated value and the true value of the quantity being measured. The error is positive if the indicated value is greater and negative if it is smaller than the true value. 2.6 Ripple Factor -- The magnitude to the arithmetic 2.6.1 Ripple arithmetic mean I ratio of the mean voltage. ripple

2.1 Rated Voltage - The output voltage at rated resistance of the tester between the `line' and the `earth' terminals, as assigned by the manufacturer. 2.2 Rated Resistance - The resistance indicated by he tester corresponding to the significant scale mark nezrest to the scale mark of infinity. 2.3 Effective Range of Measurement - That of the scale where measurement can be made the stated accuracy. part with

The periodic value. The

deviation from the magnitude of the

IS : 2992 - 1987

ripple is defined as half the difference between the maximum and the minimum values. 2.7 Indicator - The permanent magnet moving coil indicator or ratio type indicator, used to indicate directly the insulation resistance values. 2.8 Scale Length - The length of the arc through the tips of the shortest scale mark. In case of multiscale instrument, the scale length shall correspond to the longest of all scales. 2.9 Short Circuit Current - The dc current which passes through `earth' and `line' terminals when short circuited if the minimum scale marking is zero and in case minimum scale marking is other than zero, current which passes through `earth' and `line' terminal when a resistance corresponding to minimum scale mark is connected. 2.10 Type Test - Tests carried out to prove conformity with the requirements of this specification. These are intended to prove the general qualities and design of a given type of tester. Tests carried out on samples taken from a lot for the purpose of acceptance of the lot. 2.12 Routine Tests - Tests carried out on each tester to check the requirements likely to vary during production. 3. RATINGS
3.1 The rated resistance and rated 2.11 Acceptance Tests -

robust to withstand mechanical vibrations and shocks. Its working parts shall be housed in a case which shall be dustproof and of sufficient strength to afford adequate protection against external damage. 4.2 Terminals -- The tester shall be equipped with A guard a guard ring around the line terminal terminal shall also be provided and electrically connected to the guard ring in case of testers having rated resistance of I COOMC1and above. The line terminal, guard ring and the guard terminal shall be connected to the negative side and the earth terminal to the positive side of the generator. The line terminal, guard terminal and the earth terminal shall be suitably marked, preferably as L, G and T, respectively to distinguish them. 4.3 Infinity Adjustment - Testers having rated resistance 1 000 M0 and above may be provided with a suitable device accessible from out side for adjusting the pointer to the infislity mark.
NOTE Infinity adjuster may not be required in case where effective guarding of the instrument and protection against atmospheric humidity is incorporated in the instrument.

4.4 Pointer - The pointer shall have a knife-edge tip and shall be long enough to reach at least onethird of the length of the small scale marks. 4.5 Central Scale Mark - The central scale mark shall preferably be located approximately in the centre of the total effective range. 5. EFFECTIVE RANGE OF TESTER 5.1 The effective range of the tester shall be from the rated resistance donn to one-thousandth of the rated resistance. 6. ROTATION SPEED 6.1 The rotation speed of the handle at which the rated terminal voltage is attained shall not exceed 160 rev/min. It shall be ensured that the terminal voltage is within the tolerances specified in 9.2 even when the rotation speed of the handle exceeds these values. 7. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 7.1 Operation of the Tester 7.1.1 The handle of the tester shall work smoothly. It shall preferably fold back into the casing when the tester is not in use. 7.1.2 The friction in the moving system of the tester shall be the minimum possible. 2

10.2 Information and Circuit Diagram - Detailed operating instructions for using the tester, circuit diagram and precautions to be taken at the time of using the instrument, and at the time of storing, shall be supplied as accompanying documents. 10.3 The insulation resistance tester may also be marked with the Standard Mark.
NOTE - The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered bv an Indian Standard convevs the assurance that-they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and Quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standards as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

The deviation of the pointer at the infinity and zero or minimum value marked shall not exceed f 0'7 percent of the scale length. 9.2 Terminal Voltage - The terminal voltage, from rated speed up to and including 150 percent of the rated speed of rotation marked on the tester, shall be: a) within f 10 percent of the rated corresponding to the rated resistance, and bj not less than 90 percent of the rated voltage for the central scale mark. 10. error of the tester shall not exceed the limits specified in 9, after recovery, after an exposure of 24 hours to a relative humidity of 90 to 95 percent and at a temperature of 27" f 2�C. Recovery period shall be 24 h. 11.6.4 Error Due to Stray Field - The error of the tester at the central mark shall not exceed f 5 percent of the indicated value when the tester is exposed to a magnetic field produced by 400 ampere-turns (dc) in a coil of one metre diameter. The tester shall be so placed as to make the influence of the field maximum. 11.6.5 Ripple at Measuring Terminal - The ripple factor at the measuring terminai shall not exceed 10 percent. 11.7 Mechanical Endurance Test - After repetition of the starting ( up to rated speed ) and stepping the generator for 10 000 times, there shall be no evident deterioration and impairment in the working of the tester and it shall satisfy the requirements given in 9. 11.8 Dust Test 11.8.1 The chamber for this test shall be capable of maintaining, in any region inside it whe.e the tester may be placed, a temperature of 40 f 2�C and a relative humidity of not greater than 80 percent. 11.8.2 The atmosphere within the chamber shall be agitated so as to keep it loaded with dust particles of such a size as to enable them to pass through a 150-micron IS Sieve with an aperture of 0'15 mm [see IS : 460 (Part I)-1978"]. The bulk of material of dust shall consist of free silica. The concentration of dust shall be determined by means of the device described in Appendix B where the requirement of dust concentration is also specified. 11.8.3 The tester shall be placed in the test chamber for four hours with the atmosphere stirred and the dust shall then be allowed to settle for two hours. The tester shall then be removed from the chamber and shall satisfy the requirements given in 9.
11.9 Vibration Test 11.9.1 The vibration test [see IS : 1248 (Part I)1983t] shall be carried out on the insulation resistance tester. The vibration severities shall be as given below:
*Specificaticn for test sieves: sieves ( second revision ). Part 1 Wire cloth test

11.4 Insulation Resistance Test - The insulation resistance of the tester across all the external terminals connected together and the containing case and across all the external terminals connected together and the handle, when measured by applying rated dc voltage with a minimum of 500 V dc, shall be not less than the values given below: a) For rated voltage up to 25 ML1 and including 250 V 50 MQ b) For rated voltage above 250 V The voltage shall be applied for a duration long enough to get a steady reading of the insulation resistance.
11.5 High Voltage Test 11.5.1 No breakdown, arcing 0; sparking shall occur when an ac voltage of 2 000 volts (rms) is applied between all the live terminals connected together and the case for a period of one minute. 11.5.2 The value of 2 000 volts shall be applicable provided:

a) The maximum steady state output current does not exceed 5 mA ac and 10 mA dc or the mixed current 10 mA, peak; and b) The rated output voltage is up to and including 1 000 volts dc. In all other cases, the test shall be conducted at voltage equal to rated output voltage plus 1 000 volts ( U + 1 kV where U is the rated output voltage ). 11.6 Test for Limits of Error 11.6.0 Tests shall be done to prove conformity to the provision laid down in 9.1 and 9.2 and those given below. 11.6.1 Error Due to Variation of Level - A change of 5 degrees in the level of the tester, in any direction, shall not result in the deviation of the pointer from its initial position exceeding 0'5 mm. 11.6.2 Error Due to Variation of Ambient Temperature - The deviation of the indication of the tester shall not exceed 5 percent near the central scale mark for the ambient temperature change by f 20�C from 27�C.

11.12 Dry Cold Test - This test shall be carried out in accordance with IS : 9000 (Part 2/Set 1 to 3)-1977t. The meter shall be subjected to a temperature of -1Of3"C for a period of 24 hours. After a recovery period of 24 hours, the limits of error shall not exceed the values specified in 9.

SAMPLING OF INSULATION RESISTANCE TESTERS A-l. SCALE OF SAMPLING A-l.1 In any consignment, all the insulation resistance testers of the same rated resistance manufactured from the same raw material under similar conditions of production shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. A-l.2 The number of insulation resistance testers to be selected from a lot shall depend upon the lot size and shall be in accordance with co1 I and 2 of Table 2. A-1.2.1 These testers shall be selected from the lot at random. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, procedure given in IS : 4905-1968* may be followed.

APPENDIX ( Clause 11.8.2 )
DUST CHAMBER AND APPARATUS

B
DUST CONCENTRATION

FOR MEASURING

B-l. DUST CHAMBER B-l.1 A schematic layout of a typical chamber recommended for use for the dust cycle is shown in Fig. 1. It is designed to ensure uniform and reproducible distribution of dust. The system is completely enclosed and does not become conA circulating fan F (low gested during operation. pressure, high volume ventilating pattern), blows air over the pile P where the dust is picked up and carried along into the chamber C. The air velocity decreases in the chamber so that, much of the dust falls back into the hopper N from where it returns to the pile while the air is fed back into the fan through the top of the chamber. The dimensions of the hopper tube are

so proportioned that whatever the head of the dust pressure may be, the pile P never completely fills the main air duct. Consequently, the air flow carries away, more or less, a constant amount of dust from a pile which all the time is being replenished. B-l.2 The arrangement described under B-l.1 may be modified so as to result in a flow of dust loaded air which takes the shape of a rising vertex. For this purpose, four dust jets may be used in a symmetrical configuration. B-l.3 The more important details dust chamber are given below: a) Internal chamber b) Heater size rating of of a typical

91'5 cm cube 750 watts 7 100 litres/min at a pressure of 3'8 cm Ha 0, 250-watt, 3 000 rev/min meter.

B-2.1 A simple measuring device is shown in Fig. 2. Dus, enters the box through five circular holes and collects at the bottom of the detachable cover. For measuring dust concentration, the device is placed in any representative position within the dust chamber. The air is circulated for five minutes and the dust is then allowed to settle down. The amount of dust which collects on the detachable cover during the total test period is weighed and shall be 23315 g.
